items.stem: Why are signals the idiomatic way for Godot nodes to communicate about events?

options.text: They decouple the emitter from the receiver, so nodes do not need direct references to each other
options.rationale: Correct: signals enable loose coupling, like an observer pattern.

options.text: They make the game render faster
options.rationale: Signals are about structure, not rendering speed.

options.text: They replace the need for the scene tree
options.rationale: The scene tree still organises nodes.

options.text: They are the only way to move a node
options.rationale: Movement is done via code/physics, not signals.

items.explanation: Correct: signals enable loose coupling, like an observer pattern.

items.stem: What is the benefit of turning a group of nodes into a reusable scene and instancing it?

options.text: You can spawn many copies and update them all by editing the source scene
options.rationale: Correct: instancing promotes reuse and consistency.

options.text: It permanently merges the nodes into one node
options.rationale: Instancing keeps them as reusable units.

options.text: It disables scripts on those nodes
It prevents the scene from being edited

items.explanation: Correct: instancing promotes reuse and consistency.

items.stem: Which statements about Godot's node and scene system are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A scene is a tree of nodes that can itself be instanced inside other scenes
Scripts are attached to nodes to give them custom behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: GDScript (or other) extends node behaviour.

options.text: Nodes cannot be arranged in a hierarchy
options.rationale: False; the scene tree is hierarchical.

options.text: Every game must be a single node with no children
options.rationale: False; games are composed of many nodes/scenes.

items.explanation: Correct: scenes compose hierarchically.; Correct: GDScript (or other) extends node behaviour.
